item.title: Past Conference
item.description:
Completed events are collected here for reference. For upcoming meetings and ongoing seminar series, see Statistics, ML & AI events.

2026

Atlanta and nearby Georgia

  • Atlanta Mathematics of Data Science Bootcamp — September 19–20 · Georgia Tech, Atlanta. Tutorials and projects on the mathematical foundations of data science and ML, for undergraduate and high-school students.
  • ACM AI Leadership Summit — August 31–September 2 · Hyatt Regency Atlanta. AI research, agentic systems, governance, and applications across academia and industry.
  • STI Prevention Conference — August 31–September 2 · InterContinental Buckhead Atlanta. Applied public-health research on sexually transmitted infections, prevention strategies, and service delivery, connecting researchers with clinical and community partners.
  • FOPAM 2026 — July 26–30 · Courtyard by Marriott Atlanta Decatur Downtown/Emory, Decatur. Process and product analytics and machine learning. The July 26–27 pre-conference workshop connected experimental design and regression with deep learning, LLMs, and AI agents.
  • Summer Institute in Statistics and Modeling in Infectious Diseases (SISMID) — July 13–24 · Emory University, Atlanta. In-person short courses in statistical and infectious-disease modeling, including ML, MCMC, and simulation-based inference; online modules ran June 22–26.
  • Atlanta Cloud + AI Conference — May 30 · FCS Innovation Academy, Alpharetta. Practitioner sessions on cloud infrastructure, AI applications, RAG, and model deployment. See the organizer’s 2026 event packet.
  • STATGEN 2026 — May 18–20 · Emory University, Atlanta. The ASA Section on Statistics in Genomics and Genetics conference, co-organized by Emory’s Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, on statistical methodology for genomic and genetic data.
  • 11th Workshop on Biostatistics and Bioinformatics — May 8–10 · Georgia State University, Atlanta. Organized by Yichuan Zhao, with research talks and student posters. Yong Chen’s May 8 short course covered federated learning for collaborative health research using PDA and the MOSAiC framework.
  • CDC Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) Conference — April 21–24 · Atlanta. Applied epidemiology, disease investigations, and public-health data analysis. The organizer links to the 2026 agenda, presentation abstracts, and recorded sessions.
  • Atlanta AI Week 2026 — April 20–22 · Atlanta Tech Village, Buckhead. Enterprise AI, practical workshops, and startup networking.
  • Georgia State Undergraduate Research Conference (GSURC) — April 6 · Student Center East, Atlanta. Undergraduate research, scholarship, and creative projects across disciplines.
  • INFORMS Optimization Society Conference — March 20–22 · The Ritz-Carlton, Atlanta. Optimization for data science, decisions under uncertainty, and computational methods.
  • Computational Cognition Conference (CoCo Con) — March 13 · Georgia Tech, Atlanta. Computational approaches to cognition and their connections with AI.
  • Southeast Regional Clinical & Translational Science Conference — March 11–13 · Callaway Resort and Gardens, Pine Mountain, Georgia. Georgia CTSA’s regional meeting connected clinical and translational researchers. The 2026 program included medical AI implementation, clinical prediction, imaging, and LLM applications.
  • Georgia CTSA BERD Research Forum — January 30 · Georgia Tech, Atlanta. The Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Research Design forum focused on artificial intelligence in medical and health care systems, with research presentations and graduate-student posters.

Elsewhere

  • ASA/IMS Spring Research Conference — May 26–28 · Clemson University, South Carolina. A regional option beyond Georgia for research in statistics and its applications.
  • Design and Analysis of Experiments — May 19–21 · Rutgers University, New Jersey. Research on experimental design and analysis.

Notes

Updated September 26, 2026. These events had concluded by this update. Dates, venues, and descriptions are retained from the linked organizers’ or host institutions’ pages; some event websites may later switch to a newer edition.

item.title: Statistics, ML & AI events
item.description:
Places to share research, meet collaborators, and follow developments in statistics, biostatistics, bioinformatics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence around Atlanta. The directory includes upcoming research conferences, applied workshops, student presentations, and ongoing seminar series, with health-related events covering clinical research, epidemiology, biomedical imaging, and biomolecular design.

Upcoming research conferences and workshops

2026

  • IEEE International Workshop on Machine Learning for Signal Processing (MLSP) — September 28–October 1, 2026 · Georgia State University, Atlanta. Statistical learning and signal processing, including generative models, multimodal learning, and biomedical applications. Venue: Centennial Hall.
  • Georgia Statistics Day — October 5, 2026 · Georgia Tech, Atlanta. A regional statistics meeting with research talks and student posters, connecting statistics with applications across disciplines.
  • Emory AI for Health Symposium — December 4–5, 2026 · Emory University, Atlanta. The fourth symposium on AI in medicine and health, at 1760 Haygood Drive NE.
  • NeurIPS 2026 — Atlanta satellite — December 9–13, 2026 · Georgia World Congress Center, Atlanta. Main-conference sessions and tutorials run December 9–11; workshops follow December 12–13. See the venue information and the official list of 26 Atlanta workshops. Topics include uncertainty-aware decisions, evaluation of agents, reliable clinical simulation, and biomolecular design. Sydney hosts the main meeting December 6–12, while Atlanta and Paris have their own local programs.
    • World Models for High-Stakes Health — December 12. Clinical-trial simulation, treatment-effect estimation, causal inference, and uncertainty quantification using longitudinal patient data; rooms C208–C209.
    • Agentic Intelligence for Medical Imaging and Multimodal Clinical Data (AIM-NeurIPS) — December 12. AI agents that combine medical images, clinical records, and analysis tools, with an emphasis on evaluation, reliability, and human oversight.
    • Generative and Experimental Perspectives for Biomolecular Design (GEM) — December 13. Generative models, active learning, and experimental validation for proteins, molecules, and nucleic acids; relevant to computational biology and drug discovery.
  • Machine Learning & the Physical Sciences — December 11, 2026 · Georgia Tech, Atlanta. Hosted by the AI4Science Center, this independent workshop connects machine learning with physical-science research. It is near the NeurIPS venue but is not an official NeurIPS workshop in 2026.

2027

  • Suddath Symposium — March 3–4, 2027 · Georgia Tech, Atlanta. Experimental, computational, and AI approaches to predictive biomedical models, drug development, and toxicity assessment. Venue: Petit Biotechnology Building, Suddath Seminar Room 1128.
  • APHL ID Lab Con — March 15–18, 2027 · Hyatt Regency Atlanta. An applied public-health laboratory conference with tracks on pathogen genomics, infectious-disease outbreaks, and surveillance. The March 15 Advanced Molecular Detection workshop covers metagenomic sequencing, bioinformatics workflows, and genomic epidemiology. Abstracts are due October 2, 2026.
  • SIAM Conference on Applications of Dynamical Systems (DS27) — May 23–27, 2027 · Hilton Atlanta. Includes data-driven and AI-informed dynamical systems, stochastic dynamics, and scientific applications.
  • ACM Federated Computing Research Conference (FCRC) — June 5–11, 2027 · Hyatt Regency Atlanta. Co-located computing conferences connect statistical modeling, learning theory, simulation, and computing systems. Relevant meetings include:
    • STOC 2027 — June 6–11. Theory of computation, including a day on theoretical computer science and AI.
    • SIGMETRICS 2027 — June 7–11. Measurement, statistical modeling, and performance analysis of computing systems.
    • SIGSIM-PADS 2027 — June 9–11. Simulation methods and systems for modeling complex processes.
    • SPAA and PLDI — parallel algorithms and programming-language research during FCRC week; useful for researchers working on scalable ML and AI systems.

Student research and regional networking

These events offer opportunities to present work and meet researchers or practitioners across disciplines.
